newsitem.title: USA: CBOT AUGUST SOYBEANS UP SHARPLY ON TIGHT SUPPLIES.
newsitem.headline: CBOT AUGUST SOYBEANS UP SHARPLY ON TIGHT SUPPLIES.

text.p: CBOT August soybeans rose sharply Wednesday in response to tight supplies and export demand for U.S. soybeans, traders and analysts said.
"People just aren't finding the beans they need in the pipeline," one Chicago analyst said.
Supplies of soybeans are scarce at ports on the U.S. Great Lakes and at the Gulf, traders and cash sources said.
One exporter in Toledo, Ohio, estimated that 90,000 tonnes of soybeans would be needed to meet the needs of vessels heading to port, but soybean supplies in that area were low.
At 1215 CDT, August soybeans were 27-1/4 cents per bushel higher at $7.71, and other months were 3-1/2 to 10-1/4 cents higher.
